title: differential growth (coral)
notes: Algorithmic morphogenesis. Closed polyline evolves under (1) repulsion from nearby vertices via spatial hash, (2) spring attraction toward immediate neighbors on the curve, (3) small Brownian noise. When two consecutive vertices drift further than MAX_D apart, a midpoint is inserted (subdivision) — this is what makes the line GROW. Cap at 4000 vertices. Older vertices sink along -Y so the resulting form has 3D depth (coral-like ridges). 40k render particles distributed across the polyline every frame, length-weighted. Palette: bright algae (young) → coral red (mature) → bone (oldest). Click to pause/resume the growth. Watch for the second and third bifurcations — that's when the form starts feeling biological.
